claim: 14 brand-new premium morph/transition primitives, Slider-Revolution-class or better, each visually distinct from the existing 312-tile catalog. All carry the subject's own look (texture/color) — no invented placeholder fills.

q1_defects.answer: Yes, several objective defects. (a) Two tiles animate a blank featureless tan-brown placeholder sheet with zero subject content — no orange title bar, no text rows, no dot anywhere in the arc: cylinder-unroll (idle through play-3 is a flat brown fill) and genie-suck (idle sheet is also skewed and clipped at the top frame edge at rest). (b) cylinder-unroll's roll cylinder extends past the sheet and runs the full frame height as a brown stripe. (c) swap-flip-morph's alternate face is a featureless putty-grey slab — reads as an untextured quad / missing content. (d) mask-iris-morph's mask never conceals the card content: with the iris CLOSED at t=0 the orange bar, all three text rows and the blue dot are fully visible floating without the panel; at mid-open, content outside the star aperture is still visible. (e) morph-into-card's docked chip has a visible rectangular ghost plate behind the rounded pill and the chip is dimmed to near-background. (f) sdf-shape-morph shows a double-exposure mid-morph (faded rect card content + ghost disk simultaneously) and its circle/hexagon phases are flat featureless dark fills. (g) cross-morph's card is clipped at the right frame edge at peak travel. (h) Four labeled controls produce zero (or near-zero) pixel change at the engaged mid-state, and liquid-stretch-morph's stretch-sweep frames show the subject ~85% off-frame.

q2_reads_as.answer: Split. FIVE tiles read exactly as claimed and look premium: metaball-merge (cream/brass liquid blobs with smooth-union necks coalescing into the true card), flip-morph (corner thumbnail leaps to full layout; anisotropic counter-scale visible as the squashed dot mid-flight), domain-warp-morph (marbled liquid channels consume and re-form the card), pill-morph (rect breathes into a fully-rounded capsule and back), silhouette-glow-morph (fill drains to a glowing golden outline, holds, refills). NINE do not fully read as claimed: cylinder-unroll and genie-suck animate an invented blank-brown placeholder, directly contradicting 'all carry the subject's own look — no invented placeholder fills'; swap-flip-morph's 'alternate face' is a blank grey slab, not a designed second identity; mask-iris-morph does not read as an iris reveal because nothing is ever hidden; skeleton-resolve has no skeleton/ghost state — the real content is fully visible at t=0 under a diagonal sheen, so it reads as a gloss sweep (close to the existing pointer-shine look, hurting the 'visually distinct from the 312-tile catalog' claim); sdf-shape-morph's silhouette does morph (clean hexagon exists) but the surface look does NOT ride along — circle/hex phases are featureless dark fills; cross-morph's A-B-A recede/dip/advance arc is measurable and reads correctly, though its trough behavior is unverifiable (see q3).

q3_discoverable.answer: Mostly yes — the majority of labeled sliders produce immediate, visible, sensible change at the engaged mid-state (metaball-merge blend/glow/balls/speed/duration all strong; domain-warp warpStrength/flowSpeed strong; swap-flip hold/duration strong). BUT four labeled controls produce zero visible change across their full low-to-high range at the captured engaged state, which to a first-time user is a dead slider: cross-morph 'trough' (both sweep frames are pure background — the subject is fully invisible at the pinned mid-state at every trough setting), cylinder-unroll 'overshoot', swap-flip-morph 'faceBias', and liquid-stretch-morph 'stretch'. If some of these are end-phase-only parameters the t=1s pin cannot certify them — either way the user evidence shows no response.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive. Motion is real and large across play frames on every tile (no dead loops), control apply latency is uniform ~0.57-0.66s in the harness, and there are zero console or network errors on a webgpu backend for all 14 bundles. The few near-static samples are legitimate hold phases of finite entrance morphs (swap-flip play-1 is the pre-trigger hold; silhouette-glow play-3 is the held outline — though that hold being near-frozen undercuts its 'living outline' wording, see flags).
evidence: metrics: frameDeltaMag peaks — genie-suck play-2 54.18, cylinder-unroll play-2 35.03, swap-flip-morph play-2 27.75, metaball-merge play-1 20.6, domain-warp-morph play-2 18.3

q5_net.answer: ANNOYED, at the wave level. A first-time user would say: 'Five of these are genuinely gorgeous — the mercury merge, the corner-thumbnail leap and the liquid-marble dissolve feel like premium motion design. But three of them turn my card into a blank brown or grey slab with none of my content on it, the camera-iris one never actually hides anything, the skeleton one is just a shine sweep over my already-loaded card, and four of the sliders do literally nothing. I can't trust this set as shipped.' The headline claim — all 14 carry the subject's own look, no invented placeholder fills — is contradicted on camera by three tiles, so the wave cannot pass as a unit.
